Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs

Redwood to share security/compliance pack (SOC2, ISO docs, KMS integration guide)
Follow-up meeting to review benchmark results and recommended model variant
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-22 15:00 PDT | Duration: 54m | Attendees: Jamie Park (Redwood AE), Arun Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (LifeCare CTO), Ethan Gomez (ML Eng), Sofia Reyes (Head of Data)

[00:00] Jamie (Redwood): hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm jamie park from redwood, arun my se is here as well, we'll walk through the model catalog and how you might pick open models for your NLU and triage workflows.
[00:12] Maya (LifeCare): great thanks, we appreciate it. main thing for us is accuracy on clinical notes and also cost given volume, so curious what you recommend.
[00:20] Arun (Redwood-SE): yeah, totally. quick agenda, we'll show the catalog UI, talk benchmarks (latency/throughput/quality), coverage matrix for hardware and quantization, and then some optimize tips (batching, kv cache).
[00:32] Ethan (LifeCare): quick Q up front - we currently run embeddings + a smaller classification head, mostly on prem on gpus (A100s) and sometimes on cloud for peak. interested in hosted for dev but need private for PHI.
[00:45] Jamie: that matches a lot of other customers. Redwood supports hosted, dedicated reserved pools and private VPC deployments. for PHI you can do private with KMS and audit logs, we'll share SOC2/ISO pack after.
[00:58] Sofia: timeline wise we want a pilot in april, and if bench looks good we could commit to dedicated reserve later.
[01:05] Arun: good, we'll focus on pilot metrics then.

--- Catalog walkthrough ---
[01:20] Arun: opening the model catalog — ok so here you see curated open models, we surface perf proflies for each: token latency at 512/2048 seq, throughput on x86/gpu, and evaluation scores on a few public NLU tasks. note the profiles are ballpark — you should run your own bench against your prompts.
[01:40] Jamie: for example the 'mistral-ish-open-3b' entry shows int8 quantized perf on A100 at ~25ms median token latency at 512 context, and ~3.2 tokens/ms throughput on a single GPU, with minor quality tradeoff vs fp16 baseline.
[02:02] Ethan: sorry quick interruption, do you guys publish per-token cost estimates in the catalog?
[02:07] Jamie: yes we provide estimated cost bars using our pricing model; it's an estimate since your throughput and batching will change real unit costs.
[02:14] Maya: do you support sequence lengths beyond 2048? we have long notes sometimes 8k.
[02:20] Arun: catalog shows max tested context — many models are validated to 8k but performance varies. we also show recommended kernel paths; for >4096 we typically recommend the H100 optimized variants or chunking + summary pipelines.

--- Benchmarks & quality discussion ---
[02:45] Arun: onto benchmarks — we run two bench suites: latency/throughput microbench and eval suite on standard NLU datasets. the microbench shows p50/p95/p99 token latencies for common seq lengths and batch sizes.
[03:00] Jamie: important to call out p99 matters for interactive triage. we had a customer who moved from hosted to dedicated because p99 spiked under mixed workloads.
[03:12] Sofia: what's the compatibility matrix look like for gen models vs embeddings?
[03:16] Arun: good call. embeddings models are generally CPU-friendly or T4-friendly for lower cost; gen and chat models need more GPU oomph. in the matrix we map model families to supported hardware and recommended quantization levels (fp16, int8, int4 experimental). we'll send a csv link — it's in the notes as "compat_matrix_v2.csv".
[03:35] Ethan: and quality regressions after quantization - how do you detect/guard?
[03:40] Jamie: Redwood Optimize includes quality monitoring tied to eval prompt sets; you can set regression alerts and roll back to fp16. we also recommend A/B rollout, canary on a small % of traffic.

[04:05] Maya: on private deploy, what about KMS/HSM? encryption at rest and in use?
[04:10] Arun: we integrate customer KMS for key management, and support bring-your-own-key for model weights in private deployments. audit logs are retained per enterprise plan. we'll include the KMS integration guide.

--- Demo: selecting an open model for LifeCare NLU ---
[04:35] Arun: ok practical pick — you said you want high accuracy on clinical note classification and reasonable latency on A100. I'd narrow to two candidates: a 7B open model quantized to int8, and a 13B fp16 variant with an H100 profile.
[04:50] Jamie: the 7B int8 often hits sweet spot for cost — similar accuracy for classification tasks in our evals, much cheaper inference. the 13B is better for more complex generation but costs more.
[05:02] Ethan: can we see the eval numbers side-by-side?
[05:06] Arun: pulling up the comparison — here: precision/recall on clinical-entity-extraction-like set, and a small rouge-ish metric for summarization. the 7B int8 has -1.5 points vs 13B fp16 on the rouge metric but latency is ~40% lower.
[05:24] Maya: do you have per-token p99 numbers for the 7B int8 on A100?
[05:28] Arun: yeah p50 ~18ms, p95 ~55ms, p99 ~110ms at batch=1, 512 context. with batching of 8 that improves throughput but p99 rises for tail.
[05:40] Jamie: note that using our prefix KV cache for repeated patient prompts reduces tokens to generate and drops effective latency by 30-50% depending on reuse patterns — we call it KV cache but sometimes transcripts show "KV cash" haha.
[05:54] Ethan: ha. ok. for our traffic pattern most requests are short, so batching options are limited. what's your recommendation?
[06:00] Arun: with short requests go for lower-latency models and smaller batch sizes, and enable caching. also consider cpu embeddings + dedicated gpu for gen if you separate flows.

--- Deployment & pricing talk ---
[06:20] Jamie: on pricing — hosted dev is pay-as-you-go. for Dedicated you get reserved GPU pools and lower unit costs; we can model a committed spend if you share expected qps.
[06:34] Sofia: we can share monthly token estimate after the call.
[06:38] Jamie: perfect, we'll run numbers.

--- Security/compliance questions ---
[06:50] Maya: does Redwood provision single-tenant private control plane or is it isolated within your infra?
[06:55] Arun: private is customer VPC with a customer-controlled control plane option; we can do on-prem pack if you need full air gap. KMS integration and audit logs for enterprise.
[07:08] Maya: and data retention? we need guaranteed zero retention for PHI route.
[07:12] Jamie: yes enterprise private can be configured for no retention; hosted will have retention windows — we'll document specifics in the security pack.

--- Objections & clarifications ---
[07:30] Ethan: one thing — some open models have licensing restrictions, how do you manage that?
[07:35] Arun: we surface license metadata in the catalog, and modeling teams avoid models flagged with incompatible licenses. we'll also help validate for your legal team.
[07:44] Sofia: do you support Canary rollouts across model variants?
[07:47] Jamie: yes, built-in rollouts: canary, A/B, automatic rollback on quality regressions.

--- Closing / next steps ---
[08:00] Jamie: recap — we'll share the compatibility matrix, security pack, and pricing. Arun will run a proposed bench on A100 with the 7B int8 candidate. Ethan will send sample prompts.
[08:12] Maya: thanks, that sounds good. can we get the benchmark results in two weeks?
[08:16] Arun: yes two weeks is doable, we'll schedule a follow-up review.
[08:20] Jamie: i'll send calendar invite and attach pricing + contract.

[08:28] Maya: thanks everyone.
[08:30] (meeting ends)

Notes: transcript contains a few auto-caption errors (product names slightly off, occasional speaker mislabels). References shared during the call: compat_matrix_v2.csv (link in notes), security_pack_v1.pdf (link), pricing_estimate_draft.xlsx (link).
